info.title: Autoxide API
info.description:
REST API of Autoxide.

## Conventions

Every endpoint follows the same rules, so learning one endpoint teaches all of them.

- **Success**: a single result is `{"data": …}`; a list is `{"data": […], "pagination": {"limit", "next_cursor"}}`. Creating a record answers `201` with a `Location` header pointing to it.
- **Errors**: always RFC 9457 Problem Details (`application/problem+json`). Branch on the stable `code` field, never on `detail`. Validation problems list every invalid field of the request in `errors`, all at once.
- **Lists**: accept `limit` (1–200, default 50), `order` (`desc` or `asc`, by creation time) and `cursor`. Some lists also take `sort` to order by another field, and their own filters. To get the next page, pass `pagination.next_cursor` as `cursor` with the same `order`, `sort` and filters; `null` means last page.
- **Authentication**: endpoints that need it list the `bearer` security scheme. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. A `401` response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`; its `code` says whether the token is missing, invalid or expired. Public endpoints list an empty requirement next to `bearer`: they work without a token, and a sent token must still be valid.
- **Retries**: send `Idempotency-Key: <a random UUID>` with `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE`. Repeating the same request with the same key within 24 hours returns the first result (marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of doing it twice; a different request with a used key gets `422`, and a repeat while the first is still running gets `409`.
- **Concurrent edits**: reading a single record returns its version in `ETag`. Send it back in `If-Match` when changing the record: if someone changed it in between, the answer is `412` (code `precondition_failed`) instead of silently overwriting their change. Without `If-Match` the change is made anyway, except on endpoints that say `If-Match` is required: those answer `428` (code `precondition_required`).
- **Caching**: send the `ETag` you have in `If-None-Match` when reading again; if nothing changed the answer is `304 Not Modified` with no body.
- **Deprecation**: an endpoint being retired is marked `deprecated` here and answers with `Deprecation` (RFC 9745), `Sunset` (RFC 8594, the removal date) and `Link: <…>; rel="successor-version"` headers. Move to the successor before the sunset date.
- **Language**: send `Accept-Language` (e.g. `vi`) to get the `detail` of errors in that language; English (`en`) by default and for unsupported languages. Responses carry `Content-Language`. Codes never change with the language.
- **Rate limits**: too many requests from one address are answered with `429` (code `rate_limited`) and a `Retry-After` header giving the seconds to wait.
- **Which tenant**: on a server with many tenants, a request is served for the tenant of its credential (the token or API key); without one, for the tenant named in the header `Autoxide-Tenant: <slug or id>`, else for the tenant whose verified domain is in `Host` (behind a trusted proxy, `X-Forwarded-Host` or `Forwarded`). A tenant endpoint that cannot tell answers `400` with code `tenant_required` (for example a domain not bound to any tenant); a header naming no tenant answers `404` with code `tenant_not_found`; a header or domain of another tenant than the credential's answers `403` with code `tenant_mismatch`. A server with one tenant ignores both.
- **Tenant state**: any endpoint of a tenant may answer `403` with code `tenant_suspended` (the tenant is suspended: nothing works, reads included), `403` with code `tenant_read_only` (the tenant can only read for now: `GET` works, as do sign-in, exports and links from mails; other changes are refused; MCP tools that are not read-only too) or `503` with code `tenant_maintenance` and a `Retry-After` header.
- **Request id**: every response carries `x-request-id`. Send your own to correlate calls; quote it when reporting a problem.
- **IDs** are UUIDv7 strings; **timestamps** are UTC in RFC 3339; **money** is an integer amount in the smallest currency unit plus a currency code.

post.summary: Run an action on many records.
post.description:
Requires the permission of the action, and an `Idempotency-Key`. Send either `ids` (up to 500)
or `filter` with `expected_count`: when the records matching `filter` now are not
`expected_count`, nothing is done (409 `kernel.bulk_count_changed`). The action runs in a
background job with your permissions, checked on each record: follow it with
`GET /api/v1/kernel/jobs/{id}`; its `result.items` says what happened to each record (`ok`,
`skipped` with a reason, `failed` with the error `code`). With `dry_run`, nothing is done: the
answer lists the records it would act on.

parameters.description: The list, as `x-autoxide-list`, e.g. `content.list_content_entries`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The action, e.g. `archive`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required: a random UUID per bulk request.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Language of the `detail` of errors: `en` (the default) or `vi`. Codes never change with the language.

200.description: With `dry_run`: the records it would act on.

Location.description: Where the new record is, e.g. `/api/v1/auth/users/<id>`.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

403.description: Missing the permission of the action; code `permission_denied`.

404.description: No such action on this list; code `kernel.bulk_action_not_found`.

409.description: The records matching `filter` are not `expected_count` any more; code `kernel.bulk_count_changed`.

422.description: Invalid request (both or neither of `ids` and `filter`, too many records, missing `Idempotency-Key`); see `errors`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

post.summary: Add a domain to this tenant.

Requires `kernel.domains.manage`. The domain starts `pending`: set the returned DNS `record`
(TXT `_autoxide-challenge.<domain>`) at your DNS provider, then call
`POST /domains/{id}/verify` (pending domains are also checked every 10 minutes for 7 days).
Point the domain itself (A/AAAA or CNAME) at the platform's server. Adding a domain the tenant
already has returns it unchanged; retry safely with an `Idempotency-Key` header. Other tenants
waiting on the same domain do not block it: the first tenant to verify gets the domain, and the
others' claims turn `failed` when they verify.

get.summary: Stream events in real time (Server-Sent Events).
get.description:
Requires sign-in, and for each event the permission its module declares (see
`stream_permission` in `GET /api/v1/kernel/modules`): the same permission as reading the record
over REST. Only events of your tenant are sent; with a permission narrower than the whole
tenant you receive only the events you caused yourself. Events marked `stream_audience` also
reach, without the permission, the users they name (e.g. the customer and the assigned agent of
a conversation). Only events a module declares streamable are sent — never raw table changes.

Each event is one frame: `id: <event id>`, `event: <event name>`, `data: {"id", "name",
"occurred_at", "subject", "actor_kind", "payload"}`. A `: ping` comment comes every 15 s.
Delivery is **at least once**: after a reconnect you may receive an event again — skip ids you
already have. Reconnect with the `Last-Event-ID` header (browsers' `EventSource` does it for
you) or `last_event_id` to receive what you missed; events are kept 7 days, and when the id is
older the stream sends `event: reset` first — reload your data over REST. The server closes a
stream after 30 minutes and when it shuts down; reconnect the same way. Disabled unless the
server sets `AUTOXIDE_EVENTS_STREAM=true`.

parameters.name: names
parameters.description:
Event names, comma-separated: `module.event`, or `module.*` for every streamable event of
the module you may see. The module catalog lists each event's `stream_permission`.

parameters.name: last_event_id
parameters.description: Resume after this event id, for clients that cannot set the `Last-Event-ID` header.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The `id` of the last event you received; the stream resumes after it.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Language of the `detail` of errors: `en` (the default) or `vi`. Codes never change with the language.

200.description: The stream, as `text/event-stream`; it stays open.

401.description: Not signed in; see `GET /api/v1/auth/me` for the codes.

403.description: You may not receive an event you named (code `permission_denied`, naming the permission), or any of them.

404.description: Streaming is disabled on this server; code `kernel.stream_disabled`.

422.description: An event does not exist or is not streamable (code `kernel.stream_unknown_event`), or `names` / `last_event_id` is invalid (see `errors`).

429.description: Too many streams are open (per user, per tenant or on this server); code `kernel.stream_too_many`.

503.description: The server is shutting down; connect again; code `shutting_down`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

get.summary: Receive events and send live signals over a WebSocket.
get.description:
The two-way companion of `GET /api/v1/kernel/events/stream` (Server-Sent Events, still the
choice for browsers): the same events, permissions and resuming. Sign in as for REST (a bearer
token or an API key in `Authorization`); the handshake answers the same errors as the event
stream. Every message is a JSON text frame.

From the server: `{"type": "event", "event": {"id", "name", "occurred_at", "subject",
"actor_kind", "payload"}}`; `{"type": "reset"}` (what you missed is no longer kept: reload your
data over REST); `{"type": "subscribed", "names": […]}`; `{"type": "joined", "topic", "online":
[user ids]}`, `{"type": "left", "topic"}`; `{"type": "signal", "topic", "user_id", "signal":
"online" | "offline" | "typing"}`; `{"type": "pong"}`; `{"type": "error", "code", "message"}`.

From you — control messages only; writing data stays with REST: `{"type": "subscribe" |
"unsubscribe", "names": "a.b,c.*"}`, `{"type": "ack", "id"}` (the last event you processed),
`{"type": "join" | "leave" | "typing", "topic": "<kind>:<id>"}` (live signals in a topic a module
opens, e.g. a conversation; not stored), `{"type": "ping"}`.

Delivery is at least once: skip event ids you already have. Close codes: `4401` your
credentials no longer hold (token expired: sign in and reconnect), `4403` you may no longer
receive any event you named, `1012` the server restarts (reconnect with `last_event_id`).
Disabled unless the server sets `AUTOXIDE_EVENTS_STREAM=true`.

parameters.name: names
parameters.description:
Event names, comma-separated: `module.event`, or `module.*` for every streamable event of
the module you may see. Change them later with `subscribe` / `unsubscribe` messages.

parameters.name: last_event_id
parameters.description: Resume after this event id: the `id` of the last event you received.

404.description: Streaming is disabled on this server; code `kernel.stream_disabled`.

422.description: An event does not exist or is not streamable (code `kernel.stream_unknown_event`), or `names` / `last_event_id` is invalid (see `errors`).

429.description: Too many streams are open (per user, per tenant or on this server); code `kernel.stream_too_many`.

503.description: The server is shutting down; connect again; code `shutting_down`.

default.description: Any error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details. The `code` field identifies the problem.

last_error.description: For a setting of a partner connection: why its last use failed; omitted when it worked.

last_used_at.description:
For a setting of a partner connection: the last time the connection was used (or tested
with `POST /api/v1/kernel/settings/{name}/test`).

name.description:
`<module>.<key>`, e.g. `kernel.public_url`; a partner connection is named
`<module>.connection.<kind>.<field>`, e.g. `mail.connection.smtp.url`.

problem.description:
The stored value is not used any more, and why: `kernel.public_url_unverified` /
`kernel.link_unverified` / `kernel.domain_unverified` (its host is not a verified domain of this
tenant — verify the domain or change the value). Omitted when the value is used.

secret.description: Secret settings are stored encrypted and never returned: `value` is always `null`.

value.description: The value, for settings that are not secret and are set.

TenantSettingValue.description: The new value of a setting.

value.description: 1 to 4000 characters. Secret values are stored encrypted and never returned.

TenantTableRows.description: Rows of the tenant in one table.

text.description: Plain text (no HTML), 1 to 500 characters, with exactly the `{placeholders}` of the default.

TextView.description: One text a tenant may replace.

default.description: The default wording in `locale` (`null` for `ui.*` keys: the interface owns it).

legal.description: Required by law: cannot be replaced.

UpdateNoteRequest.description: Changes to a note. Omitted fields stay as they are.

UserFlag.description: A flag the interface keeps for the signed-in user, e.g. a dismissed hint.

key.description:
Lower-case letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, up to 100 characters; group flags with a
prefix, e.g. `hint.saved_views`.

value.description: Up to 200 characters, e.g. `dismissed` or the last version whose news were seen.

ViewChanges.description: Changes to a saved view; omitted fields stay as they are.

user_id.description: A user who may see the work's source; `null` removes the assignment.

counts.description: Pending work by source (the `counter` of navigation items); `work` is the total.

snoozed_until.description: Hidden from your inbox until then (only with `include_snoozed=true`).

target.description: Where to do it: the screen of `GET /api/v1/kernel/navigation` and the record.

title.description: What to do, in the language of `Accept-Language`.

WorkSnoozeRequest.description: When to show the work again.

until.description: A time in the future, at most a year away.

WorkStateView.description: The state of a piece of work for you.

snoozed_until.description: Hidden from your inbox until then.

WorkTarget.description: Where a piece of work is done.

screen.description: Screen id of the navigation, e.g. `marketing.comments`.

incomplete.description: Sources that did not answer in time or failed: the list may miss their work.

items.description: Most urgent first (`blocking`, `attention`, `info`), then soonest due.

bearer.description: A short-lived access token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
